following problem:

between any pair of sites at a certain distance for each of several

V12 for the four different groups of organisms. The other columns can
be ignored.

messages.author: 70ab9fabb9f066d8
messages.subject: Re: plot the mean and stdev of y binned for x for all series on the  same figure
parts:
Hi,

So, my first step before jumping in to binning and summarizing the
correlations, would be plotting the raw values. This isn't a huge
data set and it's important to check it makes sense to summarize them
by their mean and sd. It also helps you to think through the required
format for the data - think one row in the data frame for each point
in the plot. In which case you want each row to represent one
correlation for one distance for one population.

# get into long form
Ctest.long <- melt(Ctest, id = "distance")

# extract separate variables for population and measurement
Ctest.long <- adply(Ctest.long, 1, function(row){
unlist(strsplit(as.character(row$variable), "_"))})

# reshape to have size and correlation columns
Ctest.df <- cast(Ctest.long, distance + V1 ~ V2)

# give better names
names(Ctest.df) <- c("distance", "population", "size", "correlation")

# plot raw values
qplot(distance, correlation, data = Ctest.df) +
facet_wrap(~ population)

# I'm not convinced binning by 50000 is really what you want to do but
its easy enough to achieve

Ctest.df$dist.bin <- round_any(Ctest.df$distance, 50000)
Ctest.binned <- ddply(Ctest.df, c("population","dist.bin"), summarize,
mean.cor = mean(correlation),
sd.cor = sd(correlation))

qplot(dist.bin, mean.cor, ymin = mean.cor - sd.cor, ymax = mean.cor + sd.cor,
data = Ctest.binned, geom = "pointrange") +
facet_wrap(~ population)

Hope that helps,
Charlotte

messages.author: 70ab9fabb9f066d8
messages.subject: Re: plot the mean and stdev of y binned for x for all series on the  same figure
parts:
> (1) I would like to have a line graph with error bars for each
> population, with the error bars also having a cap (width =0.01 of the
> plot width);

see: ?geom_errorbar and you might also need geom_line if you want them
joined up across distance.

> (2) I would like to have the 6 populations plotted overlaying on each
> other, not separately in 6 sub-plots; consequently, i need to plot
> different populations in different colors and also add a legend with
> real population names like "rice", "wheat", "corn", "millet",
> "potato", and "bean", corresponding to populations 1-6 in the data;

So you don't need facet_wrap and you need to map colour to the
population variable. You probably want to change your encoding of the
population variable to the actual population names then the legend
will be correct automatically.

> (3) I also would like to label the x & y axes as "Distance" and
> "Correlation", and add a figure title;
See: ?xlab, ?ylab and use '+ opts(title = "Title")' to get an overall title.

> (4) and if possible, to get rid of the background squares used as
> scales in the plot.

See the code here: http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/book/polishing.r
Particularly the section,
# Progressively removing non-data elements from a plot with
# \f{theme_blank}.
> Could you help me to achieve all the above?
Hopefully that helps you.
